Check a region map against an independently derived assignment

Source: R/rgnmap.R
rgnmapalt.Rd

Compares the region each unit was assigned with the region a different method assigns it (a name lookup, a postal geography, an administrative list), and marks the disagreements that are already known and explained. This is the only check here that can catch an error in the method that built the map, because it does not use that method.

Usage

rgnmapalt(map, unit, reg, route, known = character())

Arguments

map

The region map, a data frame.

unit, reg

The names of its unit and region columns.

route

The second method's assignment: a vector named by unit, or a data frame with the columns unit and reg.

known

The units whose disagreement is expected and documented.

Value

A data frame of the disagreements, unexplained first: unit, primary (the map's region), second (the route's) and known. sum(!x$known) unexplained disagreements is the result, zero the pass; nrow(x) should equal the number of documented cases, as a documented case that stops disagreeing means the route changed.

Details

A second route usually has understood weaknesses: a place name that is a community rather than a municipality, an amalgamated city, a township absorbed into a neighbour. Listing them in known by name keeps the check sharp instead of loosening a tolerance until everything passes, and an unexpected disagreement cannot hide inside an allowance. Units and regions are compared as text with spaces trimmed; units the route does not cover, and route entries that are NA or blank, are skipped.

See also

rgnmapcmp(), rgnmapintg().

Examples

cw <- data.frame(inst = c("North Jail", "South Jail", "Hill Jail"),
                 cd = c("3557", "3520", "3506"))
route <- c("North Jail" = "3557", "South Jail" = "3521",
           "Hill Jail" = "3519")
d <- rgnmapalt(cw, "inst", "cd", route, known = "Hill Jail")
d
#>         unit primary second known
#> 1 South Jail    3520   3521 FALSE
#> 2  Hill Jail    3506   3519  TRUE
sum(!d$known)
#> [1] 1
try(rgnmapalt(cw, "inst", "cd", c("3557", "3520")))
#> Error : rgnmapalt: `route` must be named by unit, or be a data frame.
